clue.text: They're in rattling good -form — suggesting walkie talkie sets

definitions.text: They're in rattling good -form — suggesting walkie talkie sets

parts.words: They're in rattling good -form — suggesting walkie talkie sets
parts.note: people who rattle on in good form are great talkers, and a set of talking boxes is what a walkie-talkie pair is

explanation.surface: A review of some excellent two-way radio sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rattling good form' reads as praise for the radios, but rattling is what incessant talkers do; the walkie-talkie sets are literal boxes that chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsive talkers are called this, and the word also pictures little radio boxes that talk.

clue.text: The white one was a novel creation

definitions.text: The white one was a novel creation

parts.words: The white one was a novel creation
parts.note: Arthur Conan Doyle wrote a historical novel titled The White ___, about a band of medieval mercenaries

explanation.surface: Something white that was invented as a novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel creation' suggests something new; it means a creation in a novel, Conan Doyle's The White Company.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of soldiers or associates is a company, and The White Company is the Conan Doyle novel's title.

clue.text: Joab gave him a dig in the ribs

definitions.text: Joab gave him a dig in the ribs

parts.words: Joab gave him a dig in the ribs
parts.note: in the Second Book of Samuel, King David's general Joab stabbed Saul's commander under the fifth rib

explanation.surface: A man nudges a friend playfully in the ribs.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'dig in the ribs' sounds like a jokey nudge; in the Bible it was a fatal stab by Joab.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical commander killed by Joab with a thrust under the rib is the figure named.

clue.text: Unsavoury and in bad form

definitions.meaning: behaviour in bad form is vulgar or lacking refinement

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses of the word: without flavour, and lacking good manners or judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland food lacks flavour, and vulgar conduct lacks refinement; one word describes both.

clue.text: Sound lines of animals

indicators.note: sound here means the word for lines is to be said out loud

parts.note: lines of things are rows

explanation.surface: A good straight line of animals, perhaps at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective, healthy lines of animals, but it signals that ROWS is said out loud, giving ROES. A roe is a small deer, here in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe deer are small European deer, so the plural names a group of animals.

clue.text: In a way it takes some getting round

definitions.text: In a way it takes some getting round

parts.words: In a way it takes some getting round
parts.note: something in your way, on a path or road, that you have to get round

explanation.surface: Something that is, in a sense, hard to accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' reads as 'in a sense', but means literally in your path.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier in one's path is a hindrance that must be bypassed.

clue.text: Praise causes Roman Law to be changed

indicators.note: to be changed says the letters gathered just before are rearranged

parts.note: lex is the Latin word for law, as in the Roman lex

explanation.surface: Admiration of Roman law leads to its reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be changed' rearranges LEX plus the following TO, so 'to' is part of the fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone is to laud or glorify them, a synonym.

clue.text: Trouble with colour in America

parts.note: Americans spell the word colour without the U
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A racial or social problem in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: the American spelling of colour plus ADO gives a state in America, whose name is Spanish for red-coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: This American state takes its name from the Spanish for reddish, a colour, so the clue describes the place it builds.

clue.text: Tale of a foot ?

definitions.meaning: a tale here is a traditional story or myth
the foot is at the bottom end of the leg

explanation.walkthrough: Split the word into LEG END: that is where a foot is.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional story is a myth, and the foot sits at the lower extremity of a leg.

clue.text: Tends to provide office-bearers

definitions.meaning: to tend someone is to care for or attend to them
people holding office, such as government officials or clergy

explanation.walkthrough: One word read as a verb (attends to) and as a plural noun (holders of office in church or state).
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to people is to serve them, and cabinet members or clergy are holders of office; one word fits both.

clue.text: Change of hotel helps oarsman

definitions.note: the clue's verb phrase stands for a thing that helps an oarsman, a noun

indicators.note: a change of the word hotel means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oarsman feels better after moving to a new hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of' rearranges HOTEL. A thole is a peg on a boat's gunwale that holds the oar in place while rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: This peg acts as the pivot for an oar, so it aids the rower.

clue.text: Theirs the true Highway 'Code ?

parts.note: the sky is the true highway, so its rules belong to fliers; the Highway Code is the British driving rulebook

explanation.surface: A group of people who genuinely live by the road rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highway Code is the British book of road rules; here the highway is the air, so the code belongs to pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots and aircrew travel the air, the literal high way.

clue.text: The Muse in the Amusement Park

definitions.meaning: one of the nine Muses, the Muse of epic poetry
a steam organ heard at fairgrounds

explanation.walkthrough: The Muse of epic poetry shares her name with the steam whistle-organ of fairgrounds; note that 'Muse' sits inside 'Amusement'.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek Muse of epic poetry, and the same name is given to a fairground steam organ.

clue.text: Nodding acquaintances?

parts.note: people around you who nod in agreement to everything you say

explanation.surface: People you know only well enough to nod to.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'nodding acquaintance' is someone you barely know; here the nodding is constant agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants who always agree with a boss nod along to everything.

clue.text: As far as they can go in a beauty parlour

definitions.text: As far as they can go in a beauty parlour

parts.words: As far as they can go in a beauty parlour
parts.note: a beautician works only on the surface of the body, recalling the saying that beauty is only superficial

explanation.surface: The limits of what a beauty salon will do for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'beauty is only skin-deep' is turned literal: treatments in a salon go no deeper than the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Superficial means going no further than the outer layer of the body.

clue.text: He's never likely to be in 'the running

definitions.text: He's never likely to be in 'the running

parts.words: He's never likely to be in 'the running
parts.note: a lazy person never runs at all, so is never in contention

explanation.surface: An outsider with no chance of winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the running' means in contention; here it means actually running, which a lazy person never does.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones avoids exertion, so would never be found running.

clue.text: The last thing we wish

parts.note: the final wish someone says each day, at bedtime

explanation.surface: Something we would least want to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last thing we wish' sounds like 'what we least want'; it is the farewell wish said before bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Before sleep one bids others a peaceful night, the final greeting of the day.

clue.text: Sheriff's officer currying favour with employees?

definitions.meaning: a court officer carrying a metal-tipped staff, an old title for a bailiff
to give gratuities to the workforce, read as a phrase of verb and object

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as TIP STAFF, handing tips to staff to win their favour.
explanation.definitionFit: This bailiff carried a staff with a metal tip, and the split phrase describes giving gratuities to workers.

clue.text: Number one occasion for 'bargains, say, in canvas

parts.note: main means chief or principal, number one

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a bargains occasion is said out loud

parts.note: a sale is an occasion for bargains

explanation.surface: A big bargain sale on tents and canvas goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you SALE is heard, giving SAIL. Canvas is the traditional sail cloth, so the principal sail is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailcloth is canvas, and the principal sail on a ship's mainmast is the largest piece of it.

clue.text: Comparatively dull stuff

definitions.meaning: more matt, less shiny, as a comparative adjective

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the word as MATT-ER, more matt, a comparative of matt meaning not glossy.
explanation.definitionFit: A less glossy finish is more matt, and physical substance is stuff; one word covers both.

clue.text: Band of men, or Toc H perhaps

definitions.note: a band of soldiers, originally a Roman military unit

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the phrase might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Toc H is a Christian charity founded among soldiers in the First World War, here offered as an example of a band of men.
explanation.walkthrough: Toc H looks like the example of a band of men; with 'perhaps' it is anagram fodder: OR TOC H rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman legion's tenth part was a band of soldiers, and the word now means any group of companions.

clue.text: Would-be brownies, these workers ?

parts.note: sunbathers who want to turn brown, and also the craftsmen who cure leather hides

explanation.surface: Junior Girl Guides, the Brownies, hoping to join, described as workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are junior Girl Guides, but here 'would-be brownies' are people hoping to get a suntan; the workers are leather-curers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunbathers seek a bronzed skin, and leather workers cure hides; one word names both.

clue.text: Does it characterize a neat herd ?

definitions.text: Does it characterize a neat herd ?

parts.words: Does it characterize a neat herd ?
parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a herd of neat is cattle; the quality of being orderly is neatness

explanation.surface: Asking whether a well-kept herd of livestock is orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an archaic word for cattle, so 'neat herd' is just a herd of cattle, and neatness is the quality named.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderliness is the quality of being neat, whether of cattle or of a room.

clue.text: Mineral that can be interchanged

parts.note: the word inter, with its letters changed around, gives the mineral saltpetre

explanation.surface: A mineral that is easily swapped for another.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'interchanged' into 'inter' and 'changed': rearranging INTER gives saltpetre's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a naturally occurring mineral salt.

clue.text: Complete agreement to get old Bob into the workhouse

indicators.note: into says the old coin goes inside the word for workhouse

parts.note: a Victorian poor-law workhouse was run by a union of parishes and called the union
a bob was slang for a shilling, written s in old British money

explanation.surface: Total consensus to send an old fellow called Bob to the poorhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' is a name in the surface, but a bob was a pre-decimal British shilling, abbreviated s; a workhouse was called the union.
explanation.definitionFit: Voices in perfect accord speak or sing together as one.

clue.text: Sounds like a cunning departure in Eire

definitions.note: a place in Eire; the definition is a place there, not a phrase

indicators.note: sounds like signals that the phrase for a cunning departure is said out loud

parts.note: a cunning departure is a sly go

explanation.surface: A sly exit made somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Say SLY GO and you hear the Irish county and town. Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This town and county lie in the north-west of the Irish Republic.

clue.text: A pair of braces

parts.note: a brace means two, as in a brace of pheasants, so two braces make a count

explanation.surface: Two sets of trouser suspenders.
explanation.walkthrough: Braces are trouser suspenders in Britain, but a brace also means a pair, so a pair of braces is two twos.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is two of something, so two braces total a number.

clue.text: It happens in the course of crime prevention

indicators.note: in the course of signals letters found within the next word

explanation.surface: A crime is committed while the police are trying to prevent crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the course of' signals a run inside 'prevention'; 'crime' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence or happening is the definition's sense.

clue.text: Neighbourly team of tall men?

definitions.meaning: positioned next to, side by side
a team, or side, whose members are tall, read as three words

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as A LONG SIDE, a team of tall players.
explanation.definitionFit: Next to means beside, and a tall team would be a lengthy side.

clue.text: They're useful to those in a tearing hurry

definitions.text: They're useful to those in a tearing hurry

parts.words: They're useful to those in a tearing hurry
parts.note: rows of small holes help anyone tearing off stamps or tickets quickly

explanation.surface: Something handy for people in a great rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A tearing hurry' means a great rush; here the tearing is literal, along rows of holes in stamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows of little holes let paper be torn neatly, as between stamps.
